To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Saccharomyces HFA1 gene encodes an organelle-specific acetyl-CoA-carboxylase, which is required to maintain mitochondrial fatty-acid synthesis and, thus, to sustain the synthesis of the mitochondrial cofactor lipoic acid.
Hfa1p is a mitochondrial acetyl-Co A carboxylase that is responsible for the production of malonyl-Co A for mitochondrial fatty acid and, particularly, lipoic-acid synthesis.

(1) Hfa1p is an acetyl-CoA-carboxylase (ACC) isoform that is specifically targeted to mitochondria; (2) ACC1 and HFA1 are not functionally redundant; (3) Hfa1-encoded malonyl-CoAs provide substrates for mitochondrial lipoic acid and fatty acid synthesis.

the identification of a novel yeast mitochondrial enzyme, which is essential for the biosynthesis of mitochondrial cofactors and the maintenance of mitochondrial fatty acid pools.
the elucidation of the role of HFA1-encoded mitochondrial acetyl-Co A carboxylase in yeast fatty acid metabolism.
the characterization of a mitochondrial acetyl-Co A carboxylase in Saccharomyce cerevisiae.
